subject: Deal gating: feature tradeoffs and activation commitment for Silverline (SIL-2389)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: deal gating playbook + small runtime changes to close Silverline

Team —

Silverline (SIL-2389) is at the final procurement loop; legal sent back redlines this morning and procurement asked for two short technical commitments from us to get to signature:

1) Per-tenant compute affinity option (they want the ability to pin their tenant to a warm pool/affinity lane for 30 days after activation to avoid cold-starts during go-live). They don't need full tenancy isolation — just an affinity hint and a guaranteed warm-up window.

2) Short-term audit-log export retention flag: Silverline needs the ability to snapshot a 90-day audit export on demand for compliance reviews (they'll run 2 exports in the first 60 days). We can provide an export API but they want it as an explicit activation bullet.

Why this matters: procurement is using both asks as gating items in their SOW — if we can commit to a scoped implementation path + timeline they will sign and convert to a 12-month committed seat (anticipated $1.2M ARR). If we punt, they will escalate to competitors.

Asks: can Product/Eng provide a short playbook we can share with procurement that includes:
- A scoped description of deliverables (what we'll turn on vs what is out of scope)
- Timeline (weeks) and risk/rollback plan
- Any terms/legal language they'd need to accept (tech dependencies, temporary feature flags, etc.)

I've attached the MAP and the latest term sheet redlines from Silverline for context. Quick note: they are offering a 2-month onboarding credit in exchange for a shipping commitment within 6 weeks of signature.

Thanks — I need something we can vet internally before presenting to Nina tomorrow morning.

— Aditya
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: deal gating playbook + small runtime changes to close Silverline

Thanks for the context Aditya — appreciate the urgency. High level thoughts:

- Per-tenant compute affinity: Product is open to providing a "soft affinity" config that biases our scheduler to prefer warm hosts for matching tenant IDs for N minutes/hours after activation. That is much easier than hard pinning. We should define the exact window they want (30 days is a long period; maybe we propose an initial 14-day warm window with the option to extend under a support SLA).

- Audit export: we can support an on-demand 90-day export via the existing export pipeline; the main ask is guaranteeing the export request will be fulfilled within X hours and will not be throttled. That is largely an operational SLA.

I want Eng to weigh in on implementation effort and risk. Laura — primary asks for you: give me (a) a small-scope implementation plan we can commit to, (b) an estimate (in engineering sprints or weeks), and (c) a fallback if the feature isn't ready at the committed launch window (workarounds we can document for Silverline).

If engineering is comfortable, we'll draft a one-page playbook (deliverables + timeline + rollback) and a short paragraph of legal-friendly language for sales/legal to include in the term sheet.

— Marissa
Director, Product Management

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: deal gating playbook + small runtime changes to close Silverline

Marissa / Aditya — taking this on. Quick technical summary and proposal: 

1) Per-tenant compute affinity (proposal):
- Implement a scheduler "affinity hint" that accepts tenant_id + TTL (default 14 days). Hints will bias placement to hosts that currently have warm KV caches for that tenant. No hard pinning, no dedicated hosts.
- Implementation scope: scheduler change + light telemetry + config surface in Console + migration script to seed warm cache on activation for the first wave.
- Risk: minimal to moderate — scheduler biasing is additive but needs careful tuning to avoid starvation of other tenants. We'll guard with a circuit breaker and telemetry.
- ETA: 4 weeks to ship a guarded canary (engineering estimate: 2 engs full-time for 3 sprints; can shrink to 2 sprints with product/prioritization).
- Fallback: if not ready at go-live, ops can run a manual warm-seeding job for Silverline's activation window (1–2 hour manual task per activation).

2) On-demand 90-day audit export:
- Implementation scope: expose a one-click export on the Console and an API endpoint; add an SLA page that documents export completion expectations (e.g., 24–48 hours). This leverages the existing export pipeline.
- ETA: 2 weeks (operational/config + small UI surface). Requires a brief security review for export permission scoping.
- Risk: low; main coordination is with Security/Compliance team for retention and access control.

Constraints/notes:
- Both items are scoped to "activation assistance" not long-term architectural guarantees (we should avoid language that could be interpreted as multi-tenant isolation promises).
- We will need a short legal stub that calls these "activation-limited operational commitments" and includes an explicit out clause if the export pipeline experiences platform-wide degradation.

Next steps from Eng: I'll draft the one-page technical playbook and include the canary gating steps and rollback runbook. I can have a draft by EOD Friday (Dec 4). If sales wants the 6-week shipping commitment included in the term sheet, we should be explicit that the canary approach will allow us to meet that timeline but the full 30-day affinity extension will be "post-activation" work (we'll offer to extend via an addendum).

— Laura
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Nina Patel <nina@silverlinehealth.com>, contracts@silverlinehealth.com
Date: Thu, 04 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: deal gating playbook + small runtime changes to close Silverline

Laura / Marissa — this is perfect, thank you.

Couple of clarifications from procurement after they reviewed your notes:
- They can accept a 14-day soft-affinity with an explicit option to request an extension (we'll capture extension terms in a simple addendum).
- The on-demand export SLA of 24–48 hours is acceptable as long as it's called out in the term sheet and the MAP.

Proposal from sales side: in exchange for the guarded canary delivery within 6 weeks, Silverline will sign the 12-month commitment as-is (no additional discount). They also agreed to run the first activation during business hours and provide a primary operations contact.

Action items:
1) Laura — please share the one-page playbook + canary gating steps by EOD Friday (Dec 4).
2) Marissa — can you draft two short paragraphs for legal that describe the operational commitments (affinity TTL, export SLA, extension addendum language)? We can then add that language into the term sheet redline and share with Silverline procurement.
3) I'll update the MAP and send the signed redlines once we have those two items.

I'm attaching the MAP and the current term sheet redlines for reference. If anyone needs a call with Silverline procurement tomorrow morning, I'm happy to join.

— Aditya
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
